description: Baseline: default architecture, random init; prints the task object's public attributes (vocab/format).
Random init; prints task lengths, method signatures and sample examples to learn the prompt/answer format.
1 block, d_model=11, no MLP use: uniform attention over the prompt plus a position tilt gives the negative pinball loss; its argmax is the k-th smallest digit.
e03 with the unused MLP and ln2 deleted from Block: the model is one attention layer between embeddings and a linear head.
e04 with every LayerNorm removed: embeddings + one attention layer + linear head, identity digit head plus a position-scaled tilt column.
d_model=10: thermometer token codes make attention compute cumulative counts C_j; the head integrates k + 1/2 - C_j, whose argmax is the k-th smallest digit.
d_model=9, one channel per threshold: position lives on the all-ones direction, so the attention output is directly C_j - k - 1/2 and the head integrates it.
e07 with attention reduced to its essentials: scalar query and key projections and one output gain; W_v and W_o are deleted.
e08 with the head tied to the token embedding: logits are dot products with the thermometer codes, using the kernel 9 - max(x, d).
Separate what/where streams: one number per position sets attention scores and the rank threshold, tokens are values only, so the eps and offset workarounds are gone.
d_model=6: digit embedding is the top 6 closed-form sine eigenmodes of the min(i, i') kernel, testing how far the thermometer can be compressed.
d_model=8: top 8 closed-form sine eigenmodes of the min(i, i') kernel; one mode fewer than the exact thermometer. NOT perfect: exhaustive accuracy is 0.99837 over all 100000 inputs.
d_model=7: top 7 closed-form sine eigenmodes of the min(i, i') kernel; locates where truncation starts to hurt.
d_model=1: the multiset is packed into one base-6 number, emitted digits are subtracted, and a threshold staircase head reads off the smallest remaining digit. Autoregressive.
e14 with non-integer base 5.5: the counts no longer decode uniquely, but the leading term still dominates, so the sort should survive with a thinner margin.

e14 with base 5, past the theoretical limit: five copies of digit d+1 are worth exactly one d, so inputs of five equal digits should be misread. NOT perfect: exhaustive accuracy is 0.99992 (8 of 100000 inputs fail).
e14 in float32: tests whether subtracting emitted digits from the register loses small remainders to rounding.
Truly autoregressive thermometer sort: channels hold prompt counts minus emitted counts, position gives only a sign and gain, and it runs in float32.
e10 with attention sharpness 3 instead of 30: tests how hard the gate onto the prompt positions must be.
e10 with attention sharpness 1: attention leaks onto '=' and emitted digits, testing whether the sort survives a soft gate.
e10 with attention sharpness 0: plain uniform averaging over everything so far, with no gate on the prompt at all.
e10 with seeded Gaussian noise of std 0.05 added to the digit embeddings: robustness of the hand-written weights.
e10 with seeded Gaussian noise of std 0.01 on the digit embeddings: tests the prediction that logit error scales as noise times the norm of h.
Negative control: e10 with the tilt set to zero, so position cannot select the rank and every step should give the same answer.
e10 with random positive per-channel scales on embedding and tilt: score increments become c_j^2 * s_j, so only their signs matter and the sort should stay exact.
e10 with tilt, sharp and gain removed from the parameters: sharpness is fixed at 1 (the soft gate from e20), so the only weights are the thermometer table and one number per position.
e26 with the position table trimmed to the 10 rows that generation actually uses.
e27 with no weights for '=': its code is zero and its logit is the mean of the digit logits. 100 params: a 10x9 thermometer table plus one number per position.
e14 with both position tables trimmed to the 10 used rows: the smallest model found, d_model=1 in float64.
e18 trimmed like e28: no weights for '=', 10 position rows and a constant -1/2 offset. Rank comes only from the emitted digits, in float32.
